body.statement:
Let \(T_1,\ldots,T_n\) be independent and identically distributed random variables taking values in \(\{0,1\}\), with \(\mathbb E[T_i]=\theta\), and let \(\overline T_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nT_i\).  For every \(t>0\),
\[
\Pr\bigl(|\overline T_n-\theta|\ge t\bigr)\le 2\exp(-2nt^2).
\]

source.locator: Theorem 2, inequality (2.6), specialized to variables in the unit interval and applied to both tails

attestation.note: Transcribed from Hoeffding (1963), Theorem 2, inequality (2.6); the displayed node is its Bernoulli two-tail specialization.

body.justification: This classical finite-sample inequality controls each multinomial cell frequency.
body.gap: This is cited classical substrate, not a contribution of the note.
body.consumer: It is used only by the outer-confidence-interval proposition.
